cases.before:
`suggestion`: "legacy" names two different hashes here. The comment above calls `posthog:local_evaluation_requests:{team_id}` "the legacy local evaluation counter", but `LEGACY_LOCAL_EVALUATION_USAGE_KEY` is the new hash. At [the call site](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/9d99801364b1372ea361b8e16290ffff0c4231cd/products/feature_flags/backend/api/feature_flag.py#L4205), `increment_legacy_local_evaluation_usage` reads like it bumps the old counter.

How about naming these after Django to match the `feature-flags-django` producer (`posthog:django_local_evaluation_usage`, `increment_django_local_evaluation_usage`, `report_django_local_evaluation_usage_task`, …)? This code isn't on master yet, so the rename is free.
cases.proposed_fix: Rename only, no behavior change: `LEGACY_LOCAL_EVALUATION_USAGE_KEY` -> `DJANGO_LOCAL_EVALUATION_USAGE_KEY` with value `posthog:django_local_evaluation_usage`; `increment_legacy_local_evaluation_usage` -> `increment_django_local_evaluation_usage`; `report_legacy_local_evaluation_usage` -> `report_django_local_evaluation_usage`; `report_legacy_local_evaluation_usage_task` -> `report_django_local_evaluation_usage_task`; schedule name `report legacy local evaluation usage` -> `report django local evaluation usage`. Update the call site at `feature_flag.py:4205`, the test class name, the literal key in the API test, and `billing.md:128,132`.

facts.problem: The word "legacy" in the new names refers to a different hash than "legacy" in the comment two lines above and in the billing code, so readers will mix up the two hashes.
facts.trigger: At `feature_flag.py:4204-4205`, `increment_request_count(..., LOCAL_EVALUATION)` updates the old counter, and the next line, `increment_legacy_local_evaluation_usage`, updates the new hash that feeds usage records.
mechanism: The comment at `flag_analytics.py:34` calls `posthog:local_evaluation_requests:{team_id}` "the legacy local evaluation counter".
`LEGACY_LOCAL_EVALUATION_USAGE_KEY` on line 36 names a different hash, `posthog:legacy_local_evaluation_usage`.
In `posthog/usage_counters.py`, "legacy" means the old billing path (`UsageCounterMode.LEGACY`, "legacy totals authoritative").
facts.result: A reader of the call site will likely assume the "legacy" function updates the old counter, which is the reverse of what it does.
facts.requested_change: Name the key, the functions, the task, and the schedule entry after Django to match the `feature-flags-django` producer id, for example `posthog:django_local_evaluation_usage`, `increment_django_local_evaluation_usage`, and `report_django_local_evaluation_usage_task`.
